claim: That works out to 1,543 hours of care per caregiver per year, or nearly 30 hours a week.
sentence: This number represents an average of nearly 30 hours of care per caregiver per week, or 1,543 hours of care per caregiver per year.

figure: 25.4% (N = 55); transient misidentifications of familiar persons N = 34; of 217 outpatients
claim: In a retrospective review of the records of 217 outpatients with Alzheimer's disease, 25.4% (55) had disturbances of person identification, most often transient misidentifications of familiar people (34).
sentence: These disturbances occurred in 25.4% (N = 55) and included transient misidentifications of familiar persons (N = 34), the Capgras syndrome (N = 11), misidentification of themselves in mirrors (N = 5), prosopagnosia (N = 3), misidentification of unfamiliar persons as familiar (N = 1), and misidentification of another person as oneself (N = 1).
edition_or_date: The Journal of nervous and mental disease 180(2):94-96, 1992 (Europe PMC first publication date 1992-02-01); abstract fetched 2026-10-25
note: Read from the abstract in the Europe PMC API record (PMID 1737981, not in PMC). Title: 'Disturbances of person identification in Alzheimer's disease. A retrospective study.' Authors as listed: Mendez MF, Martin RJ, Smyth KA, Whitehouse PJ. The sentence before it gives the denominator: 'the records of 217 outpatients with AD'. The sentence after it says 'Transient misidentifications were easily corrected misperceptions'. My arithmetic: 34/217 = 15.7% of outpatients had transient misidentifications of familiar persons. 55/217 = 25.35%, which the abstract prints as 25.4%; quote the printed figure.

claim: Based on interviews with patients and their caregivers, misidentification syndromes were found in 15.8% of 392 people with probable Alzheimer's disease.
sentence: On the basis of a semistructured interview with both patients and their reliable caregivers, MIS was identified in 15.8% of cases with AD, 16.6% of patients with DLB, and in 8.3% of individuals with semantic dementia.
edition_or_date: Alzheimer disease and associated disorders 22(2):163-169, 2008 (Europe PMC first publication date 2008-04-01); abstract fetched 2026-10-25
note: Read from the abstract in the Europe PMC API record (PMID 18525289, not in PMC). Title: 'The prevalence of misidentification syndromes in neurodegenerative diseases.' Authors as listed: Harciarek M, Kertesz A. The AD group was 'Three hundred ninety-two individuals with probable AD'. The abstract also says 'The most frequent form of MIS was Capgras delusions'. My arithmetic: 15.8% of 392 is about 62 people.

claim: A meta-analysis of 8 studies pooling 1,977 people with Alzheimer's disease put the prevalence of Capgras syndrome at 6%.
sentence: Overall, a total of 1,977 patients with Alzheimer's disease were analyzed, and the prevalence of Capgras syndrome in this group was 6% (CI: 95% I² 54% 4.0-8.0).
edition_or_date: Dementia & neuropsychologia 13(4):463-468, 2019 (Europe PMC first publication date 2019-10-01); abstract fetched 2026-10-25
note: Read from the abstract in the Europe PMC API record (PMID 31844501, open access as PMC6907701). Title: 'Prevalence of Capgras syndrome in Alzheimer's patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.' Authors as listed: Pereira GCM, de Oliveira GC. Total pooled: 1,977 patients with Alzheimer's disease. The abstract also says '40 studies were identified, 8 of which were included in the present review.' The interval is printed as shown. My reading, not stated in the text, is a 95% CI of 4.0-8.0% with I-squared 54%. The open-access full text (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6907701/fullTextXML) gives the same 1,977 patients and 6% in its Results. The full text writes Alzheimer with a curly apostrophe; this API abstract uses a straight one.
